pgCapture.note: Logical replication, own publication + slot, Postgres 14+; no schema changes required.

partialSync.note: Shapes = table + WHERE + columns over HTTP; our proxy sets table and WHERE server-side, subset filters can only narrow (AND).

offlineWrites.note: Electric does no write-path sync at all; we build the outbox (PAP-272). Full control, but the cost is ours. Measured: 200 queued writes replay in 79.6 ms median in PGlite.

permissions.note: No RLS on the read path: Electric replicates as a REPLICATION role and bypasses RLS. Auth is the proxy/gatekeeper pattern, i.e. a second enforcement point beside PAP-34 RLS.

bundle.note: Client is a thin HTTP/fetch library; PGlite is a ~3 MB gzipped WASM Postgres and reserved ~540 MB RSS in the Node harness.

targets.note: Shape client is plain HTTP, runs anywhere. PGlite persistence in the Tauri WebView is IndexedDB/OPFS, which Tauri resets across app updates; treat the local DB as a cache.

selfHostLicence.note: Apache-2.0, one stateless Docker container plus a disk for the shape log. No cloud dependency.

maturity.note: 1.0 GA 2025-03-17 and shipping (1.8.1, 2026-09-07), but Electric joined Databricks 2026-08-11, Electric Cloud is winding down and future work targets Lakebase/Neon. OSS stays OSS; stewardship is the risk.

ergonomics.note: Typed shape streams, React hooks, optional TanStack DB 0.9.2 (MIT) collection layer; local store speaks the same Postgres SQL as the server.

exit.note: Plain HTTP protocol over an unmodified Postgres, and we own the write path; dropping Electric leaves the schema and the API untouched.
